newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Hambros plays down Co-op impact.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Hambros plays down Co-op impact.

text.p: British investment bank Hambros said on Wednesday its climbdown over supporting Andrew Regan in his failed takeover attempt for the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) would have an impact on new business.

"My own view is it will have an impact but it will not be long-lived...the impact will be fairly modest," Michael Sorkin, deputy chairman of Hambros Bank, told Reuters after the group reported increased pre-tax profits for 1996/97.

But, despite a dent to internal morale, Hambros had, so far, not noticed any adverse effects and Sorking said the bank, whose clients include many blue-chip companies, had received support from outside.
"We've had terrific support from our friends in the City and all our corporate customers."
Sorkin said Hambros' involvement in Regan's now discredited 1.2 billion pound takeover bid for mutually-owned supermarkets-to-funeral parlour group CWS could affect potential clients.
